topics.title: European supermarkets investigate freezer disruptions
topics.summary: Supermarkets in at least seven European countries reported refrigeration problems overnight, with several companies describing a cyberattack. The incidents renewed attention on the security of internet-connected equipment that keeps everyday retail running.
topics.discussionPrompt: A fridge hack sounds like the plot of a very strange heist movie. Which ordinary household gadget would cause the most chaos if it suddenly developed a mind of its own?

topics.title: Hungary plans to open communist-era informant records
topics.summary: Hungary is preparing to reveal names from communist-era informant files, prompting families and historians to confront difficult questions about memory, accountability and the meaning of public records decades later.
topics.discussionPrompt: If an old family box suddenly revealed a surprising chapter of local history, would you want every detail, or would some mysteries be better handled gently?

topics.title: Olympic hopefuls experiment with modern formats
topics.summary: Sports seeking a place in Brisbane 2032 are trying new formats, from obstacle courses to wearable technology. The changes show how governing bodies are balancing tradition with a push to attract new audiences.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you had to give an old sport one playful modern twist, would you add gadgets, a new setting, a shorter format, or an unexpectedly dramatic soundtrack?

topics.title: Questions raised over AI use in NHS trusts
topics.summary: A report says some NHS trusts listed as benefiting from a Palantir AI system say they use it little or not at all. The gap has sparked questions about how technology rollouts are described and measured.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a new tool is introduced at work, what makes it genuinely useful: good training, a clear problem to solve, time to learn it, or people actually asking users what they need?

topics.title: Venus, the moon and Spica line up before dawn
topics.summary: Early risers can look for Venus near the waning crescent moon and Spica, Virgo's brightest star. The close-looking trio offers a simple reason to glance skyward before sunrise this week.
topics.discussionPrompt: Are you an enthusiastic sky watcher, or do you mostly notice the stars when someone else points them out? What would get you outside before dawn?

topics.title: Scientists warn of lasting ice loss above 1.5C
topics.summary: A UN-backed report warns that even temporary warming above 1.5C could permanently damage glaciers and polar ice sheets. Researchers say the impacts could continue long after temperatures fall again.
topics.discussionPrompt: Big climate numbers can feel abstract. What helps make a long-term environmental change feel real to you: a familiar place, a photo, a personal story, or something else?

topics.title: Rare ant colony stolen from Devon reserve
topics.summary: A rare narrow-headed ant colony was taken from the only English site where the species survives, according to a Devon reserve. Conservationists say the theft has set back years of careful protection work.
topics.discussionPrompt: Nature reserves protect surprisingly tiny treasures. What small creature or plant do you think deserves far more appreciation than it usually gets?

topics.title: A weaker polar vortex may shift Europe's weather
topics.summary: Scientists are watching a disruption in high-altitude Arctic winds that could bring colder conditions to parts of Europe in coming weeks. Forecasts remain uncertain, but the polar vortex is back in the conversation.
topics.discussionPrompt: Weather science has some wonderfully dramatic names. Which forecast phrase sounds most like a band name: polar vortex, atmospheric river, thunder snow, or something you would invent?

topics.title: Tomb Raider creators revisit a gaming landmark
topics.summary: People behind the original Tomb Raider reflect on how Lara Croft and the game's success changed their lives. Their memories revisit a moment when a small team suddenly found itself shaping popular culture.
topics.discussionPrompt: Which old game, show, or gadget instantly takes you back to a particular time? Is it the story, the soundtrack, the look, or the people you shared it with?

topics.title: Festive chocolate names become a trademark dispute
topics.summary: Cadbury owner Mondelēz is challenging a vegan brand's use of a similar name for a festive chocolate treat. The row is a reminder that even cheerful seasonal snacks can lead to serious brand arguments.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you created a holiday snack, what would you call it? Bonus points for a name that sounds delicious, mildly ridiculous, and impossible to trademark.
